---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m4p5t4 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Jobs   == {1, 2, 3}
MaxCap == 3

VARIABLES queue, printed, submitted, capacity

vars == <<queue, printed, submitted, capacity>>

Range(s) == {s[i] : i \in DOMAIN s}

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ printed = {}
    /\ submitted = {}
    /\ capacity = 2

\* A fresh job is admitted only if it never entered before and there is room.
Submit(j) ==
    /\ j \notin submitted
    /\ Len(queue) < capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, j)
    /\ submitted' = submitted \cup {j}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<printed, capacity>>

\* Printing the head is the irreversible step; guarded so a job prints once.
PrintHead ==
    /\ Len(queue) > 0
    /\ LET j == Head(queue) IN
         /\ j \notin printed
         /\ printed' = printed \cup {j}
         /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<submitted, capacity>>

\* Backpressure tightens: capacity may shrink while jobs are in flight.
Shrink ==
    /\ capacity > 1
    /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, printed, submitted>>

\* Backpressure relaxes: capacity may grow up to the hard ceiling.
Grow ==
    /\ capacity < MaxCap
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, printed, submitted>>

Next ==
    \/ \E j \in Jobs : Submit(j)
    \/ PrintHead
    \/ Shrink
    \/ Grow

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A job that has already been printed is never simultaneously queued,
\* so the irreversible print of any job can happen at most once.
NoReprintQueued == \A j \in printed : j \notin Range(queue)
=============================================================================
nl:
A print shop spooler admits jobs into a bounded work queue whose capacity can be retuned while the shop is running. The Submit action admits a brand-new job only when it has never entered the spooler before and the queue still has room under the current capacity, providing backpressure. The PrintHead action performs the irreversible print of the job at the head of the queue, moving it into the printed set and dropping it from the queue, guarded so an already-printed job is never printed again. The Shrink action lowers the capacity limit (down to one) to apply tighter backpressure, and the Grow action raises the capacity limit back up to the fixed ceiling, both modelling a capacity that changes at runtime. Because the shop never re-admits a job it has already seen and print removes a job from the queue, no printed job can linger in the queue awaiting a second print.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No job that has already been printed is still present anywhere in the pending queue.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od13m7p6t1 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Machines == {1, 2}
Vals     == {0, 1}
MaxVer   == 3

\* A request is a compare-and-swap message: who sent it, the version it
\* expects to be current, and the value it wants to install.
Requests == [m : Machines, exp : 0 .. MaxVer, val : Vals]

VARIABLES reg, ver, pending, authset, log

vars == <<reg, ver, pending, authset, log>>

Init ==
    /\ reg = 0
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ pending = {}
    /\ authset = Machines
    /\ log = <<>>

\* An authorized machine posts a CAS message expecting the version it can
\* currently observe; the message then floats in the reorderable pool.
Propose(m, v) ==
    /\ m \in authset
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {[m |-> m, exp |-> ver, val |-> v]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, ver, authset, log>>

\* A message commits only if its sender is still authorized AND its expected
\* version still matches: a fresh, authorized swap.
ApplyOk(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ r.m \in authset
    /\ r.exp = ver
    /\ reg' = r.val
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ log' = Append(log, r.exp)
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED authset

\* A message whose expected version is stale is discarded, never applied.
DropStale(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ r.exp # ver
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, ver, authset, log>>

\* A message from a machine whose authorization was revoked is discarded.
DropUnauth(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ r.m \notin authset
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, ver, authset, log>>

\* Authorization can be revoked at runtime.
Revoke(m) ==
    /\ m \in authset
    /\ authset' = authset \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, ver, pending, log>>

Done == pending = {} /\ authset = {}

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machines, v \in Vals : Propose(m, v)
    \/ \E r \in pending : ApplyOk(r)
    \/ \E r \in pending : DropStale(r)
    \/ \E r \in pending : DropUnauth(r)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : Revoke(m)
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every committed swap observed a version equal to the number of swaps that
\* preceded it, so no stale participant's write ever slipped in.
FreshCommits == \A i \in DOMAIN log : log[i] = i - 1
=============================================================================
nl:
A network of vending machines shares one central register through compare-and-swap messages that can be delivered and processed in any order. The Propose action lets a currently authorized machine post a CAS message that expects whatever version it can presently observe, dropping the message into an unordered in-flight pool with a value it wants to install. The ApplyOk action commits a pooled message only when its sender is still authorized and its expected version still equals the register's live version, installing the value, bumping the version, and recording the observed version in the log. The DropStale action discards any pooled message whose expected version no longer matches the register, and the DropUnauth action discards any pooled message from a machine whose authorization has since been revoked. The Revoke action removes a machine from the authorized set at runtime. Because a swap commits only at a matching version, every logged commit observed exactly the count of swaps that came before it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every committed swap in the log observed a version number equal to the number of swaps that had already succeeded, so no stale or unauthorized write was ever applied.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od11m3p0t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

Instances == {"A", "B"}   \* two independent spooler clusters
Nodes     == {1, 2, 3}    \* candidate leaders
NoNode    == 0
Free      == "free"
MaxEpoch  == 3

VARIABLES leader, tokenOwn, tokenEp, heldEp, inCS

vars == <<leader, tokenOwn, tokenEp, heldEp, inCS>>

Init ==
    /\ leader = [i \in Instances |-> NoNode]
    /\ tokenOwn = Free
    /\ tokenEp = 0
    /\ heldEp = [i \in Instances |-> 0]
    /\ inCS = [i \in Instances |-> FALSE]

\* A leaderless cluster elects an available node as its leader.
Elect(i, n) ==
    /\ leader[i] = NoNode
    /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenOwn, tokenEp, heldEp, inCS>>

\* The elected leader grabs the free shared token, taking a fresh fence.
Acquire(i) ==
    /\ leader[i] # NoNode
    /\ tokenOwn = Free
    /\ ~inCS[i]
    /\ tokenEp < MaxEpoch
    /\ tokenOwn' = i
    /\ tokenEp' = tokenEp + 1
    /\ heldEp' = [heldEp EXCEPT ![i] = tokenEp + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, inCS>>

\* Only the token owner whose fence still matches may enter the printer.
Enter(i) ==
    /\ tokenOwn = i
    /\ heldEp[i] = tokenEp
    /\ ~inCS[i]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![i] = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, tokenOwn, tokenEp, heldEp>>

\* Leaving the printer releases the shared token back to Free.
Exit(i) ==
    /\ inCS[i]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ tokenOwn' = Free
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, tokenEp, heldEp>>

\* A leader can fail over: the cluster loses its leader and drops out of the
\* printer, but its stale recorded fence is left behind.
Failover(i) ==
    /\ leader[i] # NoNode
    /\ leader' = [leader EXCEPT ![i] = NoNode]
    /\ inCS' = [inCS EXCEPT ![i] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tokenOwn, tokenEp, heldEp>>

Next ==
    \/ \E i \in Instances, n \in Nodes : Elect(i, n)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Acquire(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Enter(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Exit(i)
    \/ \E i \in Instances : Failover(i)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Any instance actually driving the shared printer must be the current token
\* owner at the matching fence, which forces mutual exclusion of the printer.
MutexPrinter ==
    \A i \in Instances :
        inCS[i] => (tokenOwn = i /\ heldEp[i] = tokenEp)
=============================================================================
nl:
Two independent print-spooler clusters, A and B, share a single physical printer represented by one fencing token. Each cluster runs leader election with failover, and only a cluster's current leader may contend for the printer. The Elect action gives a leaderless cluster a leader chosen from the available nodes. The Acquire action lets an elected leader grab the token when it is free, bumping the token's fencing epoch and recording that epoch as the cluster's held fence. The Enter action lets a cluster begin driving the printer only when it owns the token and its recorded fence still matches the token's live epoch. The Exit action stops driving the printer and returns the token to the free state. The Failover action models a leader failure: the cluster loses its leader and drops out of the printer, but its stale recorded fence remains behind. Because only the current token owner at the matching fence can be in the printer, and the token has a single owner, at most one cluster ever drives the printer.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any cluster currently driving the shared printer must be the sole token owner at the token's current fencing epoch, guaranteeing mutual exclusion of the printer.

spec_text:
---------------------------- MODULE W4Od12m7p1t2 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals

Sites     == {"east", "west"}   \* two independent trackers on one pool
InitStock == 2
MaxVer    == 2
MaxStock  == 4

\* An idle pending slot for a site that has no read outstanding.
Idle == [active |-> FALSE, exp |-> 0, base |-> 0, delta |-> 0]

VARIABLES stock, ver, committed, pend

vars == <<stock, ver, committed, pend>>

Init ==
    /\ stock = InitStock
    /\ ver = 0
    /\ committed = 0
    /\ pend = [s \in Sites |-> Idle]

\* A site reads the shared record, snapshotting the version and stock, then
\* plans to add one unit computed from what it just read.
Read(s) ==
    /\ ~pend[s].active
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![s] = [active |-> TRUE, exp |-> ver,
                                     base |-> stock, delta |-> 1]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, ver, committed>>

\* Compare-and-swap commit: only if the snapshot version is still current does
\* the write-back (an absolute value from the stale-prone snapshot) take effect.
CommitOk(s) ==
    /\ pend[s].active
    /\ pend[s].exp = ver
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ stock' = pend[s].base + pend[s].delta
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ committed' = committed + pend[s].delta
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![s] = Idle]

\* The CAS fails because the version moved on; the site abandons its snapshot.
CommitStale(s) ==
    /\ pend[s].active
    /\ pend[s].exp # ver
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![s] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, ver, committed>>

\* A slow site simply gives up its outstanding read and will retry later.
Cancel(s) ==
    /\ pend[s].active
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![s] = Idle]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<stock, ver, committed>>

\* A trusted restock writes directly to the shared record, advancing version.
Restock ==
    /\ ver < MaxVer
    /\ stock < MaxStock
    /\ stock' = stock + 1
    /\ ver' = ver + 1
    /\ committed' = committed + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED pend

Done == ver = MaxVer /\ \A s \in Sites : ~pend[s].active

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Sites : Read(s)
    \/ \E s \in Sites : CommitOk(s)
    \/ \E s \in Sites : CommitStale(s)
    \/ \E s \in Sites : Cancel(s)
    \/ Restock
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every committed delta is fully reflected in the pool: the stock equals the
\* initial stock plus the running total of committed deltas, so no concurrent
\* update was silently lost.
NoLostUpdate == stock = InitStock + committed
=============================================================================
nl:
A blood-bank inventory pool is tracked by two independent site trackers, east and west, that share one record guarded by a compare-and-swap register. The Read action lets a site snapshot the record's current version and stock and plan to add one unit, computing the write-back from the value it just read. The CommitOk action performs the compare-and-swap: only when the snapshot's version still matches the live version does the absolute write-back from the snapshot take effect, advancing the version and adding the delta to the committed total. The CommitStale action fires when the version has moved on since the read, so the compare-and-swap fails and the site abandons its snapshot to read again later. The Cancel action lets a slow site simply give up its outstanding read and retry later. The Restock action models a trusted direct restock that writes one unit straight into the shared record and advances the version. Because a stale-snapshot write can only commit when no other update intervened, the pool's stock always equals the initial stock plus the total of every committed delta.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The pool's current stock always equals the initial stock plus the sum of all committed deltas, so no concurrent update is ever silently overwritten and lost.

---------------------------- MODULE W4Od8m9p1t3 ----------------------------
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

Students == {1, 2}
MaxEpoch == 2
MaxCap   == 2

\* An idle outbox slot for a student with no submission in flight.
Empty == [active |-> FALSE, ep |-> 0]

VARIABLES epoch, capacity, roster, log, outbox

vars == <<epoch, capacity, roster, log, outbox>>

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ capacity = 1
    /\ roster = 0
    /\ log = <<>>
    /\ outbox = [s \in Students |-> Empty]

\* A student prepares an enrollment request, tagging it with the epoch it
\* currently believes is in force.
Prepare(s) ==
    /\ ~outbox[s].active
    /\ outbox' = [outbox EXCEPT ![s] = [active |-> TRUE, ep |-> epoch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, roster, log>>

\* An enrollment is applied to the shared record only if it was prepared under
\* the epoch still in force and a seat remains.
Apply(s) ==
    /\ outbox[s].active
    /\ outbox[s].ep = epoch
    /\ roster < capacity
    /\ roster' = roster + 1
    /\ log' = Append(log, epoch)
    /\ outbox' = [outbox EXCEPT ![s] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity>>

\* A slow student's request was prepared under a superseded epoch; it is
\* rejected outright and the student may prepare again (it never fails).
Reject(s) ==
    /\ outbox[s].active
    /\ outbox[s].ep # epoch
    /\ outbox' = [outbox EXCEPT ![s] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, roster, log>>

\* A slow-but-alive student may withdraw an outstanding request and retry.
Withdraw(s) ==
    /\ outbox[s].active
    /\ outbox' = [outbox EXCEPT ![s] = Empty]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, capacity, roster, log>>

\* The registrar reconfigures: the epoch advances and seats are added, while
\* the enrollment record is carried across unchanged.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ capacity < MaxCap
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<roster, log, outbox>>

Done == roster = capacity /\ epoch = MaxEpoch /\ \A s \in Students : ~outbox[s].active

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Students : Prepare(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Apply(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Reject(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Withdraw(s)
    \/ Reconfigure
    \/ (Done /\ UNCHANGED vars)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Applied enrollments are recorded in non-decreasing epoch order, so no stale
\* request from a superseded configuration was ever folded into the record.
NoStaleApply == \A i \in DOMAIN log : i >= 2 => log[i] >= log[i-1]
=============================================================================
nl:
A university course-registration system evolves through numbered configuration epochs, and the shared enrollment record for a course is a roster of seats filled. The Prepare action lets a student submit an enrollment request tagged with the epoch it currently believes is in force. The Apply action folds a request into the shared record only when it was prepared under the epoch still in force and a seat remains, appending the epoch of that enrollment to the audit log. The Reject action discards a slow student's request that was prepared under a superseded epoch, and the Withdraw action lets a slow-but-alive student voluntarily pull back an outstanding request to retry later; in both cases the student is delayed but never failed. The Reconfigure action is the registrar advancing to a new epoch and adding seats while carrying the enrollment record across unchanged. Because only current-epoch requests are ever applied and the epoch only advances, the logged enrollments appear in non-decreasing epoch order.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The applied enrollments recorded in the audit log always appear in non-decreasing epoch order, so no stale request from a superseded configuration is ever folded into the shared record.
